# offset

<link-summary>Shifts a date by an amount of a unit.</link-summary>

<web-summary>offset() — Shifts a date by an amount of a unit. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>time</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function offset(date: Date, amount: number, unit: TimeUnit): Date;
```

A new `Date` is returned; the one passed in is untouched. A negative amount moves backwards.

Adding a month keeps the day of the month where it exists and clamps it where it does not: 31 January plus one month is 28 February, not 3 March.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type       | Description                                       |
| :-------- | :--------- | :------------------------------------------------ |
| `date`    | `Date`     | The date to read. It must be a valid `Date`.      |
| `amount`  | `number`   | How many units to move. Negative moves backwards. |
| `unit`    | `TimeUnit` | `"millisecond"` through `"year"`, as for `diff`.  |

## Returns

`Date` — a new date, shifted.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                          |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | an argument is not a valid `Date`. |

## Examples

### Shifting a date

```javascript
const start = new Date(2026, 0, 31);

offset(start, 1, "month"); // 28 February 2026 — the day is clamped
offset(start, -1, "day"); // 30 January 2026
```
